config.title: What to Wear for a Berlin Walking Tour - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers for shoes, layers, rain and a lighter walking-tour bag.

items.q: What shoes should I wear for a Berlin walking tour?
items.a: Wear supportive trainers or walking shoes with a stable, grippy sole. Central Berlin uses hard pavement and includes standing, so comfort matters more than a dressy look. Do not debut a new pair on the tour.

items.q: What should I wear for Berlin walking in the rain?
items.a: Use a removable rain layer, shoes with grip and a small bag that keeps your phone dry. Check the current forecast and the BVG connection search shortly before leaving, then shorten an exposed stretch if needed.

items.q: How many layers do I need for a Berlin walking tour?
items.a: A breathable base and one removable outer layer cover most changeable days. Add a warmer middle layer in colder months, and choose pieces you can put into a small bag when the afternoon changes.

items.q: Should I wear different clothes for a Berlin walking tour and a museum day?
items.a: Use the same comfortable shoes, then add a layer that looks fine indoors. A day around Alexanderplatz and Museum Island moves between pavement, cafés, transport and museum rooms, so adjustable clothing works better than one heavy outfit.

items.q: Is a Berlin free walking tour a good first activity?
items.a: It can be useful when you want historic context and conversation before exploring alone. BerlinWalk starts at the World Clock on Alexanderplatz and lasts about 2 hours through the historic centre of former East Berlin; check the live calendar for the current tour option.
